hypotheses.rationale: Post-2008 regulatory changes and QE suppressed equity volatility, reducing the risk premium that historically compensated momentum strategies for their crash risk; with lower vol, momentum's turnover costs now dominate, leading to underperformance vs buy-and-hold on daily SPY data after costs.
hypotheses.falsifier: A daily backtest of 12-1 momentum (long if prior 252-day return >0, else cash earning T-bill rate) on SPY data ending no later than 2025-11-10, with realistic per-trade costs (e.g. 5-10bp round-trip), shows annualized return exceeding buy-and-hold SPY.

hypotheses.rationale: Earnings quality deterioration in large-cap equities (rising accruals, lower ROE persistence) has eroded the predictive power of short-term price momentum; rational investors now demand higher compensation or avoid such signals, causing 12-1 SPY momentum to lag after daily turnover costs.
hypotheses.falsifier: A daily backtest of 12-1 momentum on SPY (signal based on 252-day return, rebalanced daily, cash in T-bills) ending no later than 2025-11-10, incorporating transaction costs, generates lower Sharpe or total return than passive SPY buy-and-hold.

hypotheses.rationale: Increased algorithmic trading and retail participation have accelerated information diffusion, shortening the half-life of momentum signals; what was once a 12-month edge now decays within weeks, making 12-1 SPY momentum unprofitable net of daily rebalancing and slippage costs.
hypotheses.falsifier: A daily backtest of 12-1 momentum (enter long SPY if 252-trading-day return positive, else T-bills) through data no later than 2025-11-10, with explicit per-trade costs, yields annualized returns below those of buy-and-hold SPY.
